topics.label: ARC — Authorization to Return to Canada
topics.seoTitle: ARC — Authorization to Return to Canada 2026 | CMG
topics.metaDescription: How to apply for an Authorization to Return to Canada (ARC) after a deportation or exclusion order — eligibility and process.
topics.h1: ARC — Authorization to Return to Canada
topics.lead: An Authorization to Return to Canada (ARC) is required for individuals previously subject to a deportation order, or an exclusion order within its applicable bar period, who wish to return to Canada before that bar would otherwise expire.

topics.label: Sponsorship Appeal (IAD)
topics.metaDescription: Appeal a refused sponsorship application to the Immigration Appeal Division — process, deadlines, and evidence strategy.
topics.lead: Most refused family sponsorship applications can be appealed to the Immigration Appeal Division (IAD), an independent tribunal that reviews the case afresh — including new evidence not seen by the original decision-maker.

topics.label: Removal Order Appeal
topics.metaDescription: Appealing a removal order to the Immigration Appeal Division — eligibility, humanitarian factors, and the appeal timeline.
topics.lead: Permanent residents and certain protected persons facing a removal order may have the right to appeal to the Immigration Appeal Division, which can consider both the legal validity of the order and humanitarian and compassionate factors.

topics.label: Residency Obligation Appeal
topics.metaDescription: Appeal a finding that you failed to meet the PR residency obligation — qualifying exceptions and the IAD appeal process.
topics.lead: Permanent residents found to have not met the 730-day residency obligation can appeal that finding to the Immigration Appeal Division, which can consider both qualifying exceptions to the residency count and broader humanitarian and compassionate factors.
headings: Common Exceptions to the Residency Count

topics.label: Judicial Review — Federal Court
topics.seoTitle: Judicial Review — Federal Court Canada 2026 | CMG
topics.metaDescription: How to seek Federal Court judicial review of a negative immigration decision — leave applications and strict filing deadlines.
topics.lead: When no appeal route is available — or an appeal has been unsuccessful — Federal Court judicial review offers a narrower form of oversight, examining whether the original decision was made reasonably and lawfully, rather than reassessing the underlying facts from scratch.

topics.label: Stay Motion
topics.seoTitle: Stay Motion Canada 2026: Federal Court | CMG
topics.metaDescription: How to file an urgent Federal Court stay motion to pause removal while a judicial review is pending.
topics.lead: A stay motion is an urgent Federal Court application to pause a removal while a related judicial review application is pending — typically filed on very short notice when a removal date is imminent.
headings: The Legal Test for a Stay

topics.label: Mandamus Application
topics.metaDescription: How a mandamus application can compel IRCC to make a decision on an unreasonably delayed immigration application.
topics.lead: A mandamus application asks the Federal Court to order IRCC to make a decision on an application that has been unreasonably delayed — used specifically for delay, not to challenge the substance of a decision that hasn't been made yet.

topics.label: Refusal & PFL Response
topics.seoTitle: Canada Visa Refusal Help 2026: GCMS, PFL & Appeals | CMG
topics.metaDescription: Refused a Canadian visa or received a Procedural Fairness Letter? GCMS notes, response strategy, and appeal options from a licensed RCIC. Urgent review.
topics.lead: Officers refuse the specific application in front of them, not an applicant's full circumstances. Requesting GCMS notes, isolating the officer's actual stated concern, and building evidence directly against that concern turns most refusals into a workable next step.
